title: WordPress & CMS Engineering

seo.title: WordPress & CMS Engineering | Julie Zimmerman
seo.description: WordPress and CMS engineering for reliable, accessible, maintainable production systems at fleet scale.

hero.headline: Building WordPress systems that remain reliable after launch.
intro: I design and maintain WordPress as an application platform, not merely a page builder.
My work spans custom plugins and themes, structured content, accessibility, migrations, security recovery, and fleet-wide operational standards across more than 250 active environments.

philosophy.title: Engineering Philosophy
philosophy.anchor: A CMS succeeds when editors can use it confidently and engineers can still understand it years later.
philosophy.intro: A reliable CMS starts with clear content models and predictable behavior.
principles: Customization should solve a real editorial or operational problem.
Accessibility, security, and maintainability belong in the architecture.
Fleet-scale work requires standards, repeatable checks, and planned retirement paths.
philosophy.closing: Fleet-scale work requires standards, repeatable checks, and planned retirement paths.

problems.title: Problems I Solve
problems.intro: The most valuable work usually begins where a system has accumulated complexity, operational risk, or assumptions no one has revisited.
items: Custom plugins, themes, blocks, and post types
Fleet-wide updates, QA, and operational consistency
WCAG remediation and accessible content structures
Malware cleanup and hardening without destroying business functionality

approach.title: How I Work
paragraphs: I begin with the publishing workflow and the system's actual constraints. I map the content model, dependencies, integrations, and failure points before choosing implementation details.
At fleet scale, one-off fixes become liabilities. I favor reusable patterns, clear ownership, conservative dependencies, and tooling that makes drift visible.

experience.summary: Lead developer and systems architect for a large, long-lived portfolio of production websites and integrations.
evidence: Technical standards, migration planning, launch QA, and incident response

experience.summary: Technical lead in enterprise higher-education software, working across large Oracle systems, performance testing, defect analysis, and release delivery.
evidence: Synthetic data generation exceeding one million records

related_writing.title: Related Writing
related_writing.intro: Case studies and essays that show the underlying engineering decisions.

business_value.title: Why durable CMS architecture matters
paragraphs: Most CMS costs arrive after launch: fragile updates, unclear ownership, inaccessible interfaces, and custom behavior no one can safely change.
A well-structured system lowers those costs by making routine work predictable and unusual failures diagnosable.

contact.title: Let's Talk
paragraphs: For technical leadership, architecture, modernization, or complex systems work, contact me directly.

closing_statement: The best CMS is not the one with the most features. It is the one people can operate safely.
